$comment: Findings that are known, attributable and accepted. The guard still prints every one of them together with its reason and tracker; they only stop failing the run. An entry that matches nothing in the tree is itself reported as a finding, so this list cannot outlive the deviation it describes. Keys are exact matches, or a prefix when they end in '*'.
$scope: These two entries accept the *shape* of the artifact -- that it ships a development JSX runtime and imports it by name. They deliberately do NOT accept anything about whether that runtime works: check 5 (jsxFactory) imports and calls the chunk on every run, so a regression to React's `jsxDEV = void 0` production stub still fails the build.
$scope2: The storage-unguarded entries accept the seven remaining unguarded storage reads, all of them on the agent-relay session path. Check 10's six repaired reads (the ones that actually ran during the first render) are NOT accepted -- they are fixed in the artifact and any reappearance is a live finding. See each entry's reason for the reachability argument.

accepted.reason: the artifact ships a development JSX runtime (jsxDEV) in a chunk named jsx-dev-runtime-*.js; the editor source that would emit jsx-runtime is not present in any public repository (docs/REPO_LAYOUT.md:17). The chunk's body was hand-repaired on 2026-09-19 to React's production element semantics (ref kept on props); the real fix is a build-config change in that private editor checkout.
same single deviation: every chunk compiled against the development JSX transform imports that chunk by name

All seven accepted unguarded storage reads are on the agent-relay session path: they pass bare `window.localStorage` into the relay's own helpers (Jy/qy/Yy), which call removeItem/setItem/getItem on it. Every one sits downstream of a guard on the relay flag (`if(!e.enabled)return`, `if(e.enabled)`) with the session object as the only key (`t.current`). `publicAgentUiEnabled` occurs exactly once in the whole artifact -- as Ux's own prop default `=!1` -- and no caller passes it, so `e.enabled` is false and these branches never execute here; the static Pages deploy also has no `/api/agent/sessions` backend (see docs/REPO_LAYOUT.md: the relay is a separate hosted service). They were deliberately left unpatched rather than hand-fixed: repairing them means rewriting session-token code that this environment cannot exercise end to end, which is a worse trade than a recorded, visible gap. The byte offsets are positions in the artifact as repaired by scripts/import-libs.json (which grows the chunk by 7653 bytes ahead of these sites); a rebuild or any further patch shifts them, at which point these entries go stale and check 10 reports the sites again for review -- which is the intended behaviour of an acceptance list, not a false alarm. It did exactly that when the import repair landed, and the offsets below were re-derived rather than re-used.
